unchecked_sentences.text: Calls: for the typical customer the predicted risk stays flat up to two calls and climbs from three: 1.2% at no calls, 1.1% at two, 2.5% at three, 9.9% at four and 66.7% at six (whole model).

The calls' direct edge (1.90 per sd) is offset while unit 4823 is on, because the calls also lower 4823, whose edge is 3.35; with more calls 4823 switches off (its value is 0.00 at three calls) and the direct edge acts alone.

Raising the typical customer's day minutes (and day charge with them), the risk is 0.9% at 200 minutes, 0.7% at 240, 52.2% at 270 and above 99% at 300 minutes without a voice-mail plan, but 0.5% at 270 and 0.4% at 300 minutes with one (469 stays at 0.00).
Below the hinge more daytime use lowers the risk slightly, through the direct day-minutes edge (-0.51 per sd).

Joint effect: heavy use also feeds 4823 and keeps it on for more calls, so the calls threshold moves up: at 270 day minutes without a voice-mail plan the risk is 52.7% at no calls and 50.9% at four, and climbs from five (71.2%).
On the training data the heavy-use detector is on for 360 customers; their churn rate is 68.3% and the model's mean predicted risk for them is 65.6%.
Of the customers with the detector on, 354 have no voice-mail plan and 6 have one.
The 318 customers with four or more calls churn at 50.0% (mean predicted 42.4%); the 3682 with three or fewer churn at 11.1%.

Concept probe: 'calls past three plus day minutes past 250 without a voice-mail plan' predicts the exit with score 0.63 (partial); the concept leaves out the evening minutes, which also feed the heavy-use detector.
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.032.
Two chained units (97 feeding 4534) and three direct edges give customers in Ohio (state code 35), Alaska (code 0) and New Jersey (code 31) their own small offsets.
The large terms nearly cancel: for the typical customer the leaf's exit is -2.92 in West Virginia, a state outside the three, against -3.19 in Ohio, -3.27 in Alaska and -2.64 in New Jersey.

So the model gives New Jersey a slightly higher churn score and Alaska and Ohio slightly lower ones: the typical customer's predicted risk is 2.8% in New Jersey, 1.5% in Alaska and 1.7% in Ohio, against 1.1% in West Virginia (whole model).
These are fitted per-state offsets: New Jersey has 90 training customers (churn rate 24.4%), Alaska 56 (7.1%) and Ohio 87 (14.9%), against 14.1% overall.
Concept probe: 'New Jersey minus Alaska minus Ohio' scores 0.99 (meaningful), a reading as three per-state offsets.
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.0027.
Two units (7285, 9021) and a direct edge on the Hawaii indicator (state code 11) give customers in Hawaii a much lower churn score.
For the typical customer the predicted risk is 0.1% in Hawaii against 1.1% in West Virginia (whole model); the leaf's exit is -3.87 in Hawaii and -0.28 elsewhere in that probe.
This is a fitted offset for 73 training customers, whose churn rate is 4.1% (overall 14.1%).
Concept probe: the Hawaii indicator scores 1.00 (meaningful).
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.0045.
Four single-state units with three direct edges give per-state offsets for Vermont (state code 46), Connecticut (6), Delaware (8), Nevada (33) and New York (34).

For the typical customer the predicted risk is 0.2% in Vermont, 0.9% in Connecticut and 1.1% in Delaware (lower), and 2.5% in Nevada and 2.7% in New York (higher), against 1.1% in West Virginia (whole model).
Vermont's offset is the largest: the leaf's exit is -2.56 there and 0.05 in West Virginia.
These are fitted offsets on small groups: Vermont 80 training customers (churn 6.2%), Connecticut 80 (17.5%), Delaware 81 (14.8%), Nevada 77 (18.2%), New York 93 (18.3%).
Concept probe: the Vermont indicator alone scores 0.83 (meaningful), since Vermont carries most of the leaf's variation.
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.0032.

For the typical customer the predicted risk is 1.4% at a 10-dollar evening charge, where unit 13517 is still off (0.00), 1.0% at 20 dollars and 0.7% at 30 dollars (whole model, evening charge changed alone).

For night calls it is 0.9% at 40 calls, 1.1% at 100 and 1.6% at 160: a direct edge (0.06 per sd) plus a hinge (unit 15132, edge 0.04) that switches on between 80 and 100 calls (its value is 0.00 at 80 and 0.43 at 100).
Concept probe: the evening charge scores 0.68 (partial); the night-calls term is not in that reading.
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.0013.

A tenure hinge: unit 4025 is off for short accounts and rises in a straight line with account length beyond a threshold; its edge to the score is 0.21, so longer-standing customers get a slightly higher churn score.
For the typical customer the unit is 0.00 at an account length of 61 and 0.14 at 91, and the predicted risk goes from 1.1% at 61 to 2.3% at 241 (whole model).
The unit is on for 2604 of 4000 training customers.
Concept probe: account length scores 1.00 (meaningful).
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.00052.
Very small offsets for the area code: a direct edge on area code 408 and a unit (9998) on area code 510.
For the typical customer the predicted risk is 1.1% in area code 408, 1.1% in 415 and 1.2% in 510 (whole model).
Concept probe: the area-code-408 indicator scores 0.94 (meaningful).
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 8e-05.
Three direct linear terms: an international plan raises the churn score (0.81 per sd), more international calls lower it (-0.21 per sd) and more daytime calls raise it a little (0.10 per sd).

For the typical customer (four international calls) the predicted risk is 1.1% without an international plan and 15.5% with one; with the plan it is 19.2% at one international call and 11.5% at eight (whole model).
On the training data the 380 customers with an international plan churn at 42.4% (mean predicted 39.6%), the 3620 without one at 11.2%.
Concept probe: the international plan scores 0.92 (meaningful).
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.002.
For the typical customer the predicted risk is 8.4% in California, 8.0% in Washington, 0.7% in Virginia and 2.2% in Idaho, whose offset is near the average (0.01) (whole model).
These are fitted offsets on small groups: California has 41 training customers (churn 26.8%), Washington 72 (29.2%), Virginia 91 (6.6%).
Concept probe: no single concept predicts the sum; the best, the Washington indicator, scores 0.20 (closed form only).
Closed form from get_formula (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate: on the training rows it is off from the exit by up to 0.0041.

Closed form from get_formula with the children expanded (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate; its leaves are each off by at most 0.032 on the training rows.
The churn score is the sum of six parts plus one tiny direct edge (area code 415) and the output bias, and the predicted risk is its sigmoid.
In order of the training AUC lost when a part is switched off: usage_service_calls (to 0.658), plan_and_calls_linear (to 0.841) and state_effects (to 0.912), from 0.920 with every part on.

Self-probe of the addition (international plan by calls, typical customer): the score is -4.45 without and -1.68 with a plan at no calls, and -2.21 and 0.56 at four calls, so the plan shifts the score by an equal amount at both call levels while the risk goes from 9.9% to 63.7% at four calls.
The typical customer used by the probes lives in West Virginia, whose own offset is below average, so the typical risks are low: the training churn rate is 14.1% and the mean predicted risk 13.4%.

Closed form from get_formula with the children expanded (coefficients rounded to three significant figures, inputs z-scored), so it is approximate; its leaves are each off by at most 0.032 on the training rows.
Customer-service calls: the predicted risk is flat up to two calls and climbs steeply from three (typical customer: 1.1% at two calls, 9.9% at four, 66.7% at six).

Heavy daytime use without a voice-mail plan switches on a heavy-use detector that raises the risk sharply (0.9% at 200 day minutes, above 99% at 300 day minutes without a voice-mail plan, 0.4% with one) and also moves the calls threshold up; below that hinge more daytime use lowers the risk slightly

An international plan adds a direct term (typical risk 1.1% without, 15.5% with), fewer international calls raise the risk, and per-state offsets, a tenure hinge and small evening, night and area-code terms add the rest.
state_direct_linear is described, not explained: a sum of per-state offsets fitted to small groups (California has 41 training customers), and the best library concept scores 0.20.

The usage-and-calls leaf reads partially (concept score 0.63): its heavy-use detector also uses evening minutes (and, weakly, night and international minutes), which the three-variable concept leaves out.
The evening and night leaf is partial too (score 0.68): the night-calls term is not in its reading.
